findings.claim: The case pattern only covers git+ssh:// and ssh+git:// by enumeration. Other ssh-transport URL forms (for example a scheme with different casing is handled by lowercasing, but variants such as git+ssh with a port or userinfo are handled by the shared host extraction only if it strips the port; the diff does not show that the host parsing handles ports, so a URL like git+ssh://localhost:2222/x would depend on code outside the diff). The new tests cover only the bare-host form for the two new schemes, with no user@ or port cases.

evidence: The change only widens the existing ssh:// case arm to two more scheme prefixes; the shared host extraction (strip scheme, strip path, strip user@) is reused unchanged, so behavior for the new schemes matches ssh://.
Tests added for localhost via git+ssh and 127.0.0.1 via ssh+git match the claimed behavior (false = not a network remote).
Host extraction after the visible lines (port stripping, loopback comparison) is not in the diff, so port or userinfo handling for the new schemes cannot be verified from here.
